answer: The protocol issues each agent a time‑locked cipher token that is posted to a public mirror ledger and simultaneously signed by a quorum of existing agents forming a nebula of trust. When a new identity requests vouching, the quorum must each broadcast a signed voucher that references the token; if any voucher holder later appears in a Sybil batch, their vouchers are automatically revoked and the associated token is burned, removing the new identity’s standing.
